tree.name: K-fold cross validation
tree.content: K-fold cross validation partitions data into k equal sized subsets, using k‑1 for training and 1 for testing, repeated k times and averaged.

details.content: K-fold cross validation partitions data into k equal sized subsets, using k‑1 for training and 1 for testing, repeated k times and averaged.

tree.name: Statistical significance test
tree.content: Statistical significance test evaluates whether performance differences between two systems are unlikely due to chance, rejecting the null hypothesis of equal efficiency.

details.content: Statistical significance test evaluates whether performance differences between two systems are unlikely due to chance, rejecting the null hypothesis of equal efficiency.

tree.name: Overfitting
tree.content: Overfitting occurs when a model captures noise and limited training examples, leading to poor generalization on unseen data.

details.content: Overfitting occurs when noise in the data and insufficient training examples cause a model to fit the training set too closely, harming generalization.

tree.name: Precision
tree.content: Precision is the proportion of correct system answers among all system answers, calculated as P = correct answers / total system answers.

details.content: Precision = number of correct system answers / number of system answers.

tree.name: Recall
tree.content: Recall measures the proportion of correct system answers among all correct problem answers, computed as R = correct answers / total correct problem answers.

details.content: Recall = number of correct system answers / number of correct problem answers.

tree.name: F1 score
tree.content: F1 score combines precision and recall into a single metric, seeking balance especially when class distribution is uneven.

details.content: F1 score seeks a balance between precision and recall and is useful when class distribution is uneven.

tree.name: Inductive bias
tree.content: Inductive bias is the set of assumptions a learner uses to predict outputs for inputs it has not encountered, enabling classification of unseen instances.

details.content: Inductive bias is the set of assumptions a learner uses to predict outputs for inputs it has not encountered.

tree.name: Maximum conditional independence
tree.content: Maximum conditional independence is an inductive bias where, in a Bayesian framework, the hypothesis is chosen to maximize conditional independence, as used by Naive Bayes classifier.

details.content: Maximum conditional independence bias suggests maximizing conditional independence in a Bayesian hypothesis, exemplified by the Naive Bayes classifier.

tree.name: Minimum cross-validation error
tree.content: Minimum cross-validation error is an inductive bias that selects the hypothesis with the lowest cross‑validation error among competing models.

details.content: Minimum cross-validation error bias selects the hypothesis with the lowest cross-validation error among alternatives.
